facts.statement: Xenoceratops was described as a new genus and species in 2012 by Ryan, Evans, and Shepherd.
facts.quote: They discovered it to be a new species and genus, and it was described in 2012 by Ryan, Evans, and Kieran M. Shepherd.

facts.statement: At the time of its description, Xenoceratops foremostensis was the oldest known ceratopsid taxon in Canada.
facts.quote: At the time of discovery, Xenoceratops foremostensis was the oldest known taxon of ceratopsid dinosaur in Canada.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous (middle Campanian stage) in what is now Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops (meaning "alien horned face") is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (middle Campanian stage), and is known to have lived in what is currently Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops lived 79 million years ago during the middle Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, hace 79 millones de años durante el Campaniano medio

facts.statement: Xenoceratops is classified as a basal centrosaurine.
facts.quote: Se trata de un centrosaurino basal.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops is distinguished from other ceratopsids by unique details of the bony ornamentation on its frill.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops can be distinguished from other ceratopsids by details of the frill's bony ornamentation.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops is apomorphic for having ovoid depressions with arched ventral margins where epiparietals contact and fuse, a trait not seen in other centrosaurines.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops es apomórfico al tener depresiones ovoidales con márgenes ventrales arqueados apareciendo en las posiciones donde los epiparietales se contactan y fusionan en los otros centrosaurinos.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops lacks the P1 process, a trait shared with other basal centrosaurines like Albertaceratops and Diabloceratops.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops también carece del proceso P1, como en otros centrosaurinos basales, como Albertaceratops y Diabloceratops, así como en los paquirinosaurinos derivados.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Xenoceratops had elongated, robust postorbital horns similar to those of other primitive, age-similar centrosaurines like Albertaceratops and Diabloceratops.
facts.quote: Por tanto, se puede inferir que Xenoceratops tenía alargados cuernos postorbitales robustos parecidos a los de otros centrosaurinos primitivos de edad similar como Albertaceratops y Diabloceratops.

facts.statement: The right P3 process is similar to all centrosaurines except some Centrosaurus specimens, but differs from all others except Albertaceratops and Medusaceratops by being broad-based and pachyostotic, and differs from those two by being straight.
facts.quote: El enorme proceso P3 derecho es similar al de todos los centrosaurinos exceptuando a algunos especímenes de Centrosaurus, aunque difiere de todos los otros centrosaurinos exceptuando Albertaceratops y el casmosaurino Medusaceratops en ser de base ancha y paquistótica, y difiere de estos dos ceratópsidos en que este proceso es recto.

facts.statement: The name Xenoceratops combines Greek xenos (foreign/alien) and ceratops (horned face), referencing the lack of known ceratopsians from its formation.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops is named from the Greek xenos, meaning foreign or alien, and ceratops, meaning horned face.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops shares with Albertaceratops and many casmosaurines the lack of bumps on the medial parietal ramus, and unlike other centrosaurines, lacks imbricated epiparietals on the lateral ramus.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops comparte con Albertaceratops y muchos casmosaurinos la carencia de "bultos" sobre el ramo medial parietal, y a diferencia de otros centrosaurinos, carece del desarrollo de epiparietales imbricados sobre el ramo lateral.

facts.statement: The species name foremostensis refers to the town of Foremost in Alberta.
facts.quote: El epíteto de la especie, foremostensis se debe al pueblo de Foremost, Alberta.

facts.statement: The name Xenoceratops comes from the Greek words xenos, meaning "foreign" or "strange", and ceratops, meaning "horned face".
facts.quote: El nombre de Xenoceratops se deriva de las palabras griegas xenos, que significa "extranjero" o "extraño", y ceratops, que significa "cara con cuernos".

facts.statement: Descriptores classified Xenoceratops in Centrosaurinae in a basal position.
facts.quote: Xenoceratops ha sido clasificado por los descriptores en Centrosaurinae, en una posición basal.

facts.statement: Xenoceratops belongs to the parent group Centrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Centrosaurinae

facts.statement: Xenoceratops is a member of the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Xenoceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Xenoceratops foremostensis is the type species of the genus Xenoceratops.
facts.quote: Type species: Xenoceratops foremostensis

facts.statement: Xenoceratops lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Xenoceratops is the oldest known Canadian ceratopsid, approximately half a million years older than Albertaceratops from the lower Oldman Formation.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, es el ceratópido canadiense más antiguo conocido, aproximadamente medio millón de años más antiguo que Albertaceratops de la Formación Oldman inferior

facts.statement: It is one of the oldest ceratopsids, about one million years younger than Diabloceratops from Utah.
facts.quote: y uno de los ceratópidos más antiguos, un millón de años más joven que Diabloceratops de Utah.
